experience.title: AI Model Evaluator & Data Specialist

details: Designed evaluation rubrics for assessing the accuracy, instruction-following, harmfulness, and writing quality of LLM responses.
Wrote political science and political theory prompts and reference answers to test multi-step deductive reasoning. Rated pairs of responses and wrote feedback for training data.
Produced RLHF preference rankings with written rationales and designed adversarial prompts to test model safety, factuality, and instruction-following.
Evaluated Chinese language model outputs for accuracy, fluency, and cultural fit, flagging localization issues.
Reviewed peer annotations across five or more projects and gave calibration feedback on how to apply project guidelines.

experience.title: Does Digital Feminism Provoke Population-Level Backlash? Evidence from the #MeToo Movement in China
experience.subtitle: Working paper presented at the Midwest Political Science Association (MPSA) Annual Conference, April 2026
details: Designed a difference-in-differences study of attitude change around China’s 2018 #MeToo movement using eight waves of the Chinese General Social Survey (2010–2023, 70,000+ pooled respondents).
Cleaned and imputed repeated cross-sectional survey data and harmonized five attitude items into a gender-egalitarianism index for consistent measurement across waves.
Assessed pre-treatment trends using event-study estimates. Used placebo public opinion outcomes and qualitative analysis to examine whether broader liberalization could explain the results.
Estimated how attitude change varied by gender and internet exposure. Found no evidence of a population-level male backlash.

projects.title: Product Search Quality Analysis
details: Built a local PySpark and Spark SQL pipeline to clean, join, and analyze 1.82 million query–product judgments from the public Amazon ESCI dataset.
Trained a search relevance classifier using 17 text-match features and logistic regression. Kept queries separate across training, validation, and test sets to prevent data leakage.
In an offline audit simulation, prioritizing low-confidence “Exact match” predictions found 32.9 errors per 100 checks, versus 19.9 expected under random sampling at the same 10% review budget.

projects.title: Amelia-Torch: Missing-Data Imputation with PyTorch
details: Implemented Amelia’s missing-data imputation method in PyTorch with CPU and GPU execution and interfaces for Python and R.

Benchmarked three public datasets of 100,000 rows each. On the 90-variable task, native PyTorch CUDA completed five imputations in 22.1 seconds, versus 230.6 seconds for serial R Amelia and 121.7 seconds with four R workers (10.43× and 5.50× speedups on the same host, RTX 3080, float64).

Built automated tests and reference comparisons to check numerical behavior and preserve observed data. Documented narrower native feature coverage, workload-specific performance, and remaining statistical validation gaps.
